desktop.limits.intro: The macOS app has 102 screens (VIEWS.md). This window implements a handful. Rather than let absence be ambiguous, everything below is named with the reason and the PARITY.md row behind it.
desktop.limits.missing.heading: NOT AVAILABLE IN THIS CLIENT
desktop.limits.missing.note: Protocol, hardware or platform facts. Nothing in this list has a control anywhere in the window, disabled or otherwise.
desktop.limits.notYet.heading: WORKS IN THE CLIENT, NOT IN THIS WINDOW YET
desktop.limits.notYet.note: A schedule, not a limit. Every one of these is reachable today from the REPL: ./oshi.sh run --args="--client"
desktop.media.caveat.animated: Animated — the first frame is shown. This window has no animation loop; playing it would need a frame clock this viewer deliberately does not have.
desktop.media.caveat.truncated: Incomplete: this file does not end the way its format requires, so part of the picture is missing and what fills that space was never sent. A download that was interrupted, or a copy that was. Ask the sender to send it again.
desktop.media.caveat.view_once: View once: you have opened this. The file stays on this disk — this client does not destroy it and the sender is never told — and it is not revealed in your file manager from here.
desktop.media.no_key: No media key is loaded in this window, so the attachment cannot be decrypted.
desktop.media.note.empty: The file on disk is zero bytes. That is a failed or interrupted write here, not a damaged message — the download deletes a partial file, so an empty one means the path was created by something else.
desktop.media.note.inline_oversize: This image is too large for this window to decode in one piece (over 16 MiB). The file is on disk and intact; open it in an image viewer.
desktop.media.note.missing_file: The decrypted file is not at that path any more. Nothing was lost on the wire — the bytes were written to this disk when the message arrived and something has removed them since.
desktop.media.note.no_header: This file does not begin with an image header this window can read — truncated at the very start, or not a picture at all whatever it is called. Nothing was decoded, because there were no dimensions to decode into.
desktop.media.note.not_a_file: There is no file at that path any more. The bytes were decrypted to this disk when the message arrived; something has removed or moved them since. Nothing was lost on the wire and the sender does not need to resend for this window's sake.
desktop.media.note.not_image: These bytes are %@, which is not a still image, whatever the file is called — the name came from the sender and this is what the file itself says. This window draws still pictures and does not play anything, so there is nothing honest for it to show. The file is on disk and unchanged.
desktop.media.note.oversize: This file is %1$@, over this window's %2$@ ceiling for reading an image into memory in one piece. The file is on disk and intact; open it in an image viewer, which can decode it without holding all of it.
desktop.media.note.sealed: View once, as the sender marked it. Reveal is a LOCAL action: this client does not destroy the file afterwards and the sender is never told you opened it.
desktop.media.note.too_many_pixels: This image declares %1$@ — %2$@ megapixels, over this window's %3$@ MP decoding ceiling. Nothing was decoded: the dimensions come from the file's header. A small file that claims enormous dimensions is the shape of a deliberate attack as well as the shape of a panorama, and this window declines both the same way.
desktop.media.note.undecodable: The bytes are on disk but this window's image library could not turn them into a picture. Truncated, or a format this build of skia does not carry. That is a statement about THIS decoder and not about the file: another OSHI client, and your own image viewer, may well open it.
desktop.media.note.unparseable: This attachment reference is not in the form this window knows how to read, so it is shown verbatim rather than interpreted.
desktop.media.open_failed: Could not open a decrypted copy (%@).
desktop.media.reveal.failed: This machine's desktop refused to open the folder (%@). The path above is the file; nothing about the file has changed.
desktop.media.save_failed: The copy was not saved (%1$@); nothing was left at %2$@.
desktop.media.sig.unknown: not in a form this window recognises
